import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_67/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_67/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation History: JOIN on ["user_id", "user_id"]
# Join df0 and df1 on 'user_id' column (inner join by default)
df_joined = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# According to target schema:
# ['user_id': integer, 'timestamp': string, 'source': string, 'device': string, 'operative_system': string,
#  'test': integer, 'price': integer, 'converted': integer, 'city': string]

# Ensure columns are in the correct order and types match target schema
# Convert types explicitly if needed

# user_id: integer
df_joined["user_id"] = df_joined["user_id"].astype(int)

# timestamp: string (keep as is)
df_joined["timestamp"] = df_joined["timestamp"].astype(str)

# source: string
df_joined["source"] = df_joined["source"].astype(str)

# device: string
df_joined["device"] = df_joined["device"].astype(str)

# operative_system: string
df_joined["operative_system"] = df_joined["operative_system"].astype(str)

# test: integer
df_joined["test"] = df_joined["test"].astype(int)

# price: integer
df_joined["price"] = df_joined["price"].astype(int)

# converted: integer
df_joined["converted"] = df_joined["converted"].astype(int)

# city: string
df_joined["city"] = df_joined["city"].astype(str)

# Select columns in target schema order
df_target = df_joined[
    [
        "user_id",
        "timestamp",
        "source",
        "device",
        "operative_system",
        "test",
        "price",
        "converted",
        "city",
    ]
]

# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_67/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_67/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_67/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Perform an outer join on 'user_id' to keep all rows from source0 and enrich with city info from source1
# The target examples have more rows than the join result from the failed pipeline, so use left join to keep all source0 rows
result = pd.merge(source0, source1[['user_id', 'city']], on='user_id', how='left')

# Write the final output with exact target schema column order
result = result[['user_id', 'timestamp', 'source', 'device', 'operative_system', 'test', 'price', 'converted', 'city']]

result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_67/target_multisource_critique_history.csv")
